assessment.nobel_worthiness: Information design supplies a general and consequential framework for strategic communication and institutional design.
assessment.attribution: Bergemann, Kamenica and Morris are central to the formal foundations and development of the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established, broadly used across theory and applied fields, and its implications are increasingly visible in market design.
uncertainties: The boundaries between foundational information-design work and adjacent persuasion literature remain difficult to compress into three laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed modern trade analysis by linking selection, productivity and distributional consequences of trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the core model, with Helpman and Redding major contributors to its theoretical development and applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a large durable literature and is central to contemporary quantitative trade research.
uncertainties: Attribution overlaps with broader trade contributions by several candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of reciprocity and inequity aversion materially changed economic models of behavior, contracts and cooperation.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt made closely connected theoretical and experimental contributions to the nominated research programme.
assessment.maturity: The findings and models have been tested extensively and remain influential across economics.
uncertainties: The broad social-preferences literature makes a sharply bounded attribution challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Decision theory under ambiguity provided rigorous alternatives to expected utility for economically important uncertainty.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are central to maxmin and recursive ambiguity preferences, while Marinacci has made major foundational contributions.
assessment.maturity: These models are mature theoretical tools with sustained applications in macroeconomics, finance and strategic analysis.
uncertainties: The credited set does not fully represent all antecedents of Choquet-based ambiguity theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Network economics created powerful tools for understanding diffusion, interaction and the formation of economic relationships.
assessment.attribution: Jackson, Kranton and Goyal are leading architects of the stated theoretical programme.
assessment.maturity: The field is established and influential, with applications spanning markets, learning and policy.
uncertainties: Its breadth makes it harder to identify one discovery with the compactness typical of a prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining and related market models supplied foundational strategic tools with wide use in economic theory.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the indispensable source of the canonical bargaining model; Wolinsky and Binmore made major related contributions.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has endured for decades and remains standard in theory and applied bargaining analysis.
uncertainties: The contribution's importance may be seen as part of a wider game-theory tradition already recognized in prior prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioral game theory made controlled evidence central to the study of strategic economic behavior.
assessment.attribution: Plott, Holt and Camerer are prominent contributors to laboratory-market methods and their strategic applications.
assessment.maturity: The methods and results are long established and have shaped both theory testing and market-design practice.
uncertainties: The experimental tradition has many essential contributors, complicating a three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical models of demand and competition substantially expanded the ability to evaluate industrial and regulatory policy.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn are central to landmark approaches to dynamic industry analysis and demand estimation.
assessment.maturity: These methods are deeply embedded in industrial organization and empirical policy analysis.
uncertainties: The nomination combines several distinct methodological advances and exceeds a naturally limited attribution.
